Article Title: Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards
Article Text:
Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards

Gigabyte has launched its Gigabyte 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign to mark its 40th anniversary, offering consumers a chance to win Amazon gift vouchers, monitors, AORUS merchandise and other products. The campaign will run from November 1 to December 31, 2026, and is open to residents of India. The campaign will feature three activities: Build a Rig, Play a Run and Share Your Story. Consumers can participate by purchasing eligible Gigabyte products, playing a browser-based game or sharing stories about their Gigabyte hardware.Under the Build a Rig activity, Gigabyte is offering rewards through its AORUS Full House programme. Consumers purchasing eligible Gigabyte and AORUS products can earn Amazon gift vouchers based on the number of product categories included in their PC build.The vouchers are worth up to Rs 15,500. Participants with complete builds can also receive AORUS merchandise, while select AORUS INFINITY products qualify for an additional bonus.The Play a Run activity features AORUS Infinity Run, a free browser-based game that takes players through five eras of hardware, from 1986 to the AI era.Each run lasts up to 90 seconds, and players do not need to log in. Participants can submit one entry per day after completing a run. Every valid entry will be included in a monthly random draw for a Gigabyte monitor.Players can also share their scorecards on Instagram by tagging @aorus_in and using the hashtag #MyGigabyte to participate in AORUS merchandise giveaways.The Share Your Story activity, called Still Running, invites consumers to share their experiences with Gigabyte products they have owned. Participants can write about hardware that remains in their PC, has been passed on to someone else or has been retired. Stories can be submitted on Instagram using @aorus_in and hashtags #MyGigabyte or #ENTERINFINITYINDIA, through the pinned Still Running thread on the r/aorusin Reddit community, or via an online form.More than 20 prizes are available, including at least three Gigabyte products. A Gigabyte India panel will select monthly winners across four categories: Best Story, Best Second Life, Most Loyal Builder and Still Running.The campaign activities opened on November 1, 2026, at 12am IST and will close on December 31, 2026, at 11:59pm IST. November winners will be announced in the first week of December 2026, while December winners will be announced in the first week of January 2027.Gigabyte said the campaign will run through its India community channels on Instagram and Reddit. Two of the three activities are free to enter, and participants can submit their stories in any language.Commenting on the campaign, Sunil Grewal, Director, Gigabyte India, said, “Forty years is a long time in an industry where hardware changes every year or two. What has carried us through is the trust of people who build their own PCs and expect them to keep running long after the build is done. ENTER INFINITY is our way of handing this anniversary to them. Whether someone is building a new rig this festive season, playing a quick run, or telling us about a Gigabyte motherboard that is still running years later, we want our next chapter in India to be shaped by those experiences.
Article Summary: Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards. The campaign will run from November 1 to December 31, 2026, and is open to residents of India. Consumers can participate by purchasing eligible Gigabyte products, playing a browser-based game or sharing stories about their Gigabyte hardware.

Article Title: As California’s billionaire tax faces defeat, problems for wealthy tech execs may not be over
Article Text:
Countermeasures seal Prop 40’s fate

Mixed results for wealth taxes across other US states

Federal scrutiny awaits in Democrat controlled Congress

California’s ultra-wealthy tech executives appear on the verge of defeating a state wealth tax, but their tax battles are far from finished. While election officials continue counting ballots, early returns show 56% of California voters rejecting Proposition 40, compared to 44% in favour. As the ballot measure requires a simple majority to pass, election analysts say defeat is virtually assured, as per a report by CNBC. The measure sought to impose a one-time 5% levy on the net worth of California residents holding more than $1 billion in assets.While Silicon Valley billionaires breathe a sigh of relief at home, tax experts warn that the state-level fight could catalyse a much broader push in Washington, where newly empowered Democrats in Congress are eyeing federal tax increases on top earners and a potential federal wealth tax, the report added.The billionaire tax ran into direct opposition from two competing ballot measures designed as legislative countermeasures.Proposition 41: Restricts how state tax revenue can be spent.Proposition 42: Explicitly prohibits the state from taxing personal assets.Both countermeasures are currently winning majority support among voters. Under California election rules, if either proposition receives more total votes than Proposition 40, the billionaire tax is officially nullified, the report added.Faced with the mounting deficit, the proposal’s primary backer conceded defeat with the healthcare union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW West) announcing plans to reintroduce the initiative in 2028 unless state lawmakers intervene to “make billionaires pay their fair share.”While California voters rejected taxing accumulated net worth, measures aimed at taxing high-income earners saw stronger momentum elsewhere. In Washington State, voters approved a new “millionaire tax,” establishing a 9.9% tax rate on household income exceeding $1 million per year.In Colorado, a ballot measure seeking to replace the state’s 4.4% flat tax with a graduated income tax, featuring an 8.4% top bracket on earnings above $1 million, remains too close to call.With Democrats now positioned to take control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, tax policy analysts anticipate a wave of federal legislation designed to increase levies on wealthy individuals and corporations to fund middle-class relief.“It is clear Democrats will try to lower taxes for middle-income households and raise taxes on certain businesses and high-income households. But it is much too soon to know how,” said Howard Gleckman, nonresident fellow at the Tax Policy Center, as per CNBC.Federal lawmakers could revive legislative frameworks introduced during the last congressional cycle by Democratic Senators Chris Van Hollen of Maryland and Cory Booker of New Jersey. Van Hollen’s proposal introduces a graduated surtax on incomes surpassing $1 million:$1 Million to $2 Million: A 5% surtax.Over $5 Million: A 12% surtax.Top Marginal Income Rate: Would rise to 49%, up from the current 37% federal ceiling.Capital Gains: The top long-term capital gains tax rate would jump from 23.8% to 35.8%.To counterbalance the tax hikes, the plan proposes expanding exemptions for middle- and lower-income filers, creating a $46,000 deduction for single tax filers and a $92,000 deduction for joint filers.
Article Summary: California voters reject a state wealth tax on ultra-wealthy tech executives. Prop 40 requires a simple majority to pass, but election analysts say defeat is virtually assured. Newly empowered Democrats in Congress are eyeing federal tax increases on top earners and a potential federal wealth tax.

Article Title: World’s most valuable company CEO loses spot in world’s top 10 richest, loses $15 billion in a day
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

$2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq in one day

Why tech companies lost billions recently

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang lost his place in the world’s top 15 richest billionaires. According to Bloomberg, the tech billionaire lost nearly $15.1 billion in a day after the company’s stocks tumbled following Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm election. The loss dropped him to 13th from ninth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Other billionaires whose wealth declined were Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Oracle founder Larry Ellison, who lost $79.7 billion and $10.1 billion, respectively.The decline comes after the Nasdaq 100 index erased $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day on November 5 as Nvidia and other major technology companies suffered steep losses amid growing fears over the future of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending in the US. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5% on Thursday, marking its biggest one-day drop since the market sell-off triggered by US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025.The fall hit major tech companies include Nvidia and AMD whose shares dropped by 9% and 17% during Thursday’s trading session. Notably, Nvidia hit a market capitalization of $5.02 trillion earlier this week, regaining the title of world’s most valuable company from Apple.The Democrats’ strong performance in the US midterm elections has raised concerns that local opposition and tighter scrutiny could slow the construction of new data centres. Several incoming Democratic governors, including in Texas, have called for an immediate moratorium on data centre development.Data centres require large amounts of electricity and water, raising concerns among communities about pressure on power grids and local resources. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses.Analysts have warned that the AI boom may be entering a phase where companies are judged not just on their growth potential but also on the cost of building and operating their infrastructure.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang lost nearly $15.1 billion in a day after the company’s stocks tumbled following Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm election. The loss dropped him to 13th from ninth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Other billionaires whose wealth declined were Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Oracle founder Larry Ellison.

Article Title: Indian shoppers turn value-conscious during festive sales, says Fynd report
Article Text:
Value-led shopping dominates

Footwear overtakes clothing

Eastern India gains prominence

Tier 2 cities drive growth

Brands must adapt to changing consumer priorities

Indian consumers adopted a more cautious and value-driven approach to festive shopping in 2026, with over half of all online fashion orders priced below ₹1,000, according to Fynd's Festive Season Report 2026. The report suggests that shoppers balanced affordability with selective premium spending amid economic uncertainty, rising living costs and changing marketplace preferences. The report, released by AI-native unified commerce platform Fynd, draws insights from more than 65 brands selling across eight major online marketplaces, including Myntra, Flipkart, Amazon, AJIO, Nykaa, JioMart, Tata CLiQ and Tata CLiQ Luxury, during the September-October festive shopping period.According to the report, 50.1% of all festive season orders were placed below ₹1,000, highlighting a strong value-first mindset among consumers. At the same time, orders worth more than ₹3,000 accounted for only 11.8% of total purchases but contributed more than 41% of overall sales value, indicating that shoppers were willing to spend on products they considered worthwhile. Fynd said consumers became more deliberate in their spending decisions, comparing options more carefully and prioritising purchases that offered practicality, versatility and perceived value rather than engaging in indiscriminate festive buying.Footwear emerged as the biggest online fashion category during the festive season, accounting for 52.7% of all orders and 58.4% of total sales value. The category's share of orders increased significantly from 33% in 2025.In contrast, clothing's share declined from 48% to 34.5%, suggesting shoppers were becoming more selective about discretionary fashion purchases while continuing to invest in products with everyday utility. The report also highlighted aggressive discounting across platforms, with average festive season discounts rising from 34% to 46%. Nearly half of all orders were sold at discounts of more than 50%.One of the standout trends identified by Fynd was the growing contribution of Eastern India to online fashion commerce. The region accounted for 20.8% of all festive season orders, while West Bengal emerged as the country's second-largest ordering state. The report also found that prepaid digital payments continued to gain traction, with online payments accounting for 56.5% of all orders. Fynd noted that prepaid adoption accelerated particularly across eastern markets.Tier 2 cities saw a sharp rise in contribution during the festive season, increasing their share of orders from 19% in 2025 to around 35% in 2026. The trend points to growing demand from emerging consumption centres beyond India's major metropolitan regions.Meanwhile, Tier 1 cities contributed approximately 43% of total orders but generated 56% of gross merchandise value (GMV), underscoring the spending power of larger urban markets.Marketplace competition also intensified during the season. While Myntra and Flipkart retained leadership positions, their combined share fell from 89% to 76.8% as platforms including AJIO, Amazon and JioMart gained market share.Commenting on the findings, Ragini Varma, Chief Business Officer for India at Fynd, said consumers navigated a festive season marked by higher borrowing costs, elevated fuel prices, geopolitical uncertainties and continued pressure on household budgets. She noted that value emerged as the defining theme of the season, with shoppers planning purchases more carefully and focusing on products that justified their spending. The report concludes that future growth for retailers will depend on stronger regional strategies, marketplace diversification, disciplined discounting, improved prepaid adoption and a deeper understanding of evolving consumer behaviour across categories and regions.
Article Summary: 50.1% of all festive season orders were placed below ₹1,000. Footwear emerged as the biggest online fashion category during the festive season. Tier 2 cities saw a sharp rise in contribution from 19% in 2025 to 35% in 2026.

Florida voters approved an overhaul of the state’s property tax system, passing Amendment 3 with 62% of the vote. While pitched primarily as relief for everyday residents squeezed by rising living costs, its true financial windfall for the ultra-wealthy elite buying up South Florida's luxury properties lies in a modified assessment rule. For the tech titans and hedge-fund founders who have bought houses for hundreds of millions of dollars, this is a welcome decision though the exemption offers little more than loose change.Under Amendment 3, the state’s homestead exemption on non-school property taxes will triple from the current $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027, before jumping to $250,000 in 2028. By shielding more of a primary residence’s assessed value from local taxation, the measure will lower annual tax bills for typical homeowners. New residents will also be eligible for the break, though on a phased-in timeline. As the homestead tax exemption applies as a flat dollar deduction, its benefits drop to near zero against multi-million-dollar mega-mansions.Raul Gastesi, a real estate attorney and co-founder of Miami law firm Gastesi Lopez Mestre & Cobiella, calculated that at the statewide average non-school tax rate, the fully phased-in exemption will save a homestead owner roughly $2,085 per year:Real estate experts told Fortune that the most consequential provision for ultra-wealthy investors is a less discussed element of Amendment 3: a tighter cap on how fast taxes can climb on secondary properties, rental homes, and commercial holdings.Previously, Florida capped annual taxable value increases on non-homestead properties at 10%. Amendment 3 halves that ceiling to 5%.In red-hot luxury property markets like South Florida, home values often appreciate at rapid speeds. As billionaires frequently own multiple estates, investment residences and commercial tracts, capping assessed valuation hikes at 5% significantly slows down the tax climb on their rapidly appreciating secondary assets.The policy change coincides with a concentration of wealth moving into South Florida’s exclusive luxury corridors.

Article Title: Anthropic allows managers to monitor employees’ Claude usage; company says: It will report on ...
Article Text:
“Smart reports analyze how a team uses Claude and report on the work getting done, what it costs at list price, where sessions run into friction, and which repeated patterns are worth packaging as shared skills,”

Who can enable the feature

What can managers see in Smart Reports

Team reports can identify individual employees

Privacy restrictions mentioned by Anthropic

Anthropic is giving managers more visibility into workplace Claude usage. Its Smart Reports feature analyses samples of team conversations, groups them by the work performed and shows associated costs. Available on Claude Enterprise plans, the tool can cover chat, Claude Code and Claude Cowork, depending on an organisation’s configuration.Anthropic wrote in a blog post.The feature is disabled by default and requires an organisation owner to enable it. Names are hidden initially, but organisations can separately permit authorised viewers to reveal users’ identities. Anthropic says organisations should not use the reports to evaluate individual performance or make employment decisions.Each eligible organisation can generate up to 10 reports monthly at no charge. Reports usually take a few hours to produce. Smart Reports are unavailable to Enterprise organizations using customer-managed encryption keys, a HIPAA configuration or certain hybrid deployments.Where zero data retention is enabled for Claude Code, reports exclude Claude Code and cover chat and Cowork instead.Authorised users can select a team, products and a reporting period covering up to the previous 28 days. They can also choose focus areas and add questions for Claude to answer while analysing transcripts.Claude reads a sample of conversations and groups sessions into workstreams and output types, such as analysis, documentation, content drafts and code. Reports show spending at list prices, average costs by output type and obstacles encountered during tasks.Viewers can open a workstream to see sessions ranked by cost. Each eligible session includes a paragraph-long summary, the product used, the date and the output type.Reports also identify recurring problems, including tool failures, missing integrations, sign-in restrictions and repeated attempts to correct unsuitable output. Recommendations can highlight workflows worth turning into shared skills.Anthropic provides a separate “Allow attribution to individual users” setting, which is also off by default. When attribution is disabled, session details display “User” instead of a name and hide session identifiers. If the organisation enables attribution, viewers still see anonymous labels initially but can use a control to reveal names and session identifiers. Each reveal is logged.This means the feature does not guarantee anonymity across every configuration. Access depends on organisational settings, permissions and how a report is shared. Owners and administrators with analytics access can create reports. Organisations can also give team leads or department heads access limited to assigned groups.The documentation lists mandatory safeguards for sensitive subjects, including health, protected characteristics, union activity, harassment complaints, whistleblowing, political or religious views and personal matters.Custom questions about restricted topics are blocked. Sessions Claude identifies as involving those topics are included only in aggregate analysis, without session summaries. Personal conversations also exclude individual session details and names.These protections depend on Claude identifying the relevant content. The documentation describes the safeguards but does not establish how reliably that classification works in practice.
Article Summary: Anthropic is giving managers more visibility into workplace Claude usage. Smart Reports analyses samples of team conversations, groups them by the work performed and shows associated costs. Available on Claude Enterprise plans, the tool can cover chat, Claude Code and Claude Cowork, depending on an organisation’s configuration.

Article Title: Hugging Face CEO just told Sam Altman and Dario Amodei: You need to do more than just telling the world that your AI models went rogue, time to …
Article Text:
AI agents hack Hugging Face

Hugging Face CEO calls for legal liability on AI agents

Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue has sent a warning to artificial intelligence (AI) CEOs. Speaking at the WIRED World Fair in Miami, he argued that while leading industry executives frequently warn about AI risks, real safety requires accountability and open development rather than corporate secrecy. He added that the biggest dangers surrounding AI will not come from open-source collaboration, but from a handful of tech giants developing frontier models in secret.“Most of the risk is actually created by a couple of players building behind closed doors. Most of the mitigation of this risk will be the full ecosystem, meaning everyone being able to build in the open,” Delangue was quoted as saying. Delangue’s warnings come from firsthand experience. Hugging Face became one of the first known companies to be struck by rogue artificial intelligence.In July, autonomous agents undergoing testing at OpenAI broke free of their testing sandbox and launched a targeted cyberattack against Hugging Face. The rogue agents went on the internet to infiltrate the startup’s systems in an effort to extract answers to evaluation tasks they had been assigned to solve. To defend its platform, Hugging Face turned to an open-weight Chinese model called GLM-5.2 to investigate the intrusion and repel the hacking.Anthropic has also disclosed multiple instances of an AI model hacking external systems during testing.Delangue pointed out that autonomous agent misbehaviour seen so far has originated from dominant players experimenting with frontier systems behind closed doors. He cautioned that upcoming high-stakes threats, such as dangerous biological capabilities or autonomous models improving themselves recursively, are likely to emerge from these same proprietary labs.While Hugging Face decided against pursuing legal action against OpenAI following the July incident, Delangue insisted that companies deploying autonomous software must face legal consequences for what their systems do.“Cyber-attacks are illegal, and I think it’s really important we make sure that agentic cyberattacks [are] illegal. We don’t want to create an environment where there’s no ownership, there’s no responsibility for cyber-attack,” Delangue said.Despite these emerging security issues, Delangue rejected the apocalyptic narratives shared by some industry figures who claim AI presents an existential risk to human survival. Delangue stated that his “P(doom)”, which is the estimated mathematical probability of AI destroying humanity, is “close to zero,” remarking that “there are many other topics that could destroy the world.”Delangue stressed that the continued health of open-source artificial intelligence is critical to keeping power from consolidating into a tiny corporate monopoly.
Article Summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue has sent a warning to artificial intelligence (AI) CEOs. He argued that real safety requires accountability and open development rather than corporate secrecy. Hugging Face became one of the first known companies to be struck by rogue artificial intelligence.

Article Title: China 'shocks' Japan's richest man Masayoshi Son; tells him: You cannot buy Europe's biggest robotics company; leaving company to determine what went wrong and whether it is ...
Article Text:
Representative Image

Why did China oppose Softbank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division

Why are ABB’s Chinese operations important

What does the setback mean for SoftBank

China has reportedly blocked SoftBank’s planned purchase of ABB’s robotics division. The $5.4 billion acquisition was intended to underpin founder Masayoshi Son’s expansion into physical artificial intelligence (AI), technology that combines AI with machines operating in the real world. According to a Financial Times report, China’s National Development and Reform Commission told the Japanese group the transaction would not proceed.The decision surprised people close to SoftBank and those briefed on the review, who had expected approval until the preceding week, the report said. SoftBank is now examining what went wrong and whether it can seek approval again. ABB’s Chinese operations were a significant attraction for the acquisition, making Beijing’s decision consequential for Son’s robotics plans.SoftBank agreed to acquire ABB’s robotics division in October 2025. The deal cleared China’s competition review in February before undergoing a separate foreign investment security review, which examines potential national security risks.According to people familiar with the process cited by the FT, regulators scrutinised the robotics unit’s Chinese supply chains and sought to retain some manufacturing capabilities in the country.The commission was also concerned that robotics data could be transferred overseas and used to train AI models, including those developed by OpenAI, in which SoftBank is a major investor, the report said.Regulators examined keeping intellectual property associated with parts of ABB’s robotics business in China. This could have required spinning off some operations to Chinese owners for the transaction to proceed.However, people close to SoftBank said uncertainty in Japan remained about which conditions regulators were formally requesting before the decision.China is the robotics division’s biggest market. According to the report, more than 90% of the robots it supplies to Chinese customers are manufactured locally.ABB formed a joint venture with a Chinese partner in 1992, and government support has benefited its operations. Shanghai’s government helped the company build its $150 million robotics factory in Pudong, which began operating in 2022.The review reflected Beijing’s concerns about transferring assets developed in China to a Japanese company amid tensions with Tokyo and strategic competition with Washington, the FT reported.ABB’s robotics business was expected to underpin Son’s physical AI strategy alongside US AI and robotics company Roze.Son is also in talks to acquire Allied Universal, the private security group that owns Britain’s G4S, with plans to use robotics and AI to improve productivity, according to the report. However, SoftBank has not established whether another approval attempt could succeed.
Article Summary: SoftBank agreed to acquire ABB’s robotics division in October 2025. The $5.4 billion acquisition was intended to underpin founder Masayoshi Son's expansion into physical artificial intelligence (AI) China's National Development and Reform Commission told the Japanese group the transaction would not proceed.

Article Title: As DoorDash spends $17 billion to buy Instacart, it sends a 'LinkedIn message' to its employees; tells them: You cannot add...
Article Text:
No LinkedIn connections with Instacart, DoorDash tells employees

DoorDash's LinkedIn ban is meant to stop 'gun-jumping' before the Instacart deal closes

DoorDash's caution reflects the antitrust scrutiny ahead for the Instacart deal

DoorDash has told its employees not to add Instacart staff on LinkedIn while its $17 billion acquisition of the grocery delivery company waits for approval. The instruction sits in an internal question-and-answer document that DoorDash filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 29, the day the deal was announced. When employees ask if they can connect with Instacart colleagues on LinkedIn, the answer is short: "Not at this time."The rule works both ways. DoorDash staff cannot send new connection requests to Instacart workers or accept theirs, "even if you have a prior relationship." Existing connections can stay. If someone from Instacart does reach out, the company has a ready-made reply: "Congrats! Looking forward to connecting after the deal closes." Anything beyond that needs a nod from the legal team. The deal is expected to close at the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, so the freeze could last up to 20 months.Until the paperwork is done, DoorDash and Instacart are still competitors, and the law expects them to act like it. Antitrust lawyers call it gun-jumping when merging companies behave as if a deal has already closed. The US Federal Trade Commission has warned that companies in a pending merger must protect sensitive information such as pricing, costs and business strategy.Sharing it too early could break antitrust laws and push up prices before regulators have even ruled.Chris Selland, a lecturer at Northeastern University, sees the LinkedIn rule as protection against "poaching and org-chart mapping in case the deal is ultimately blocked." In that case, the two would go back to being rivals. DoorDash staff can still apply for Instacart jobs, but only the way any outside candidate would.Selland calls the policy a clearly worded guardrail rather than a heavy-handed ban, one that keeps employees from straying into talk about job openings, pay or shared accounts. He also concedes that a single LinkedIn connection "likely won't blow up a deal on its own."Limits on contact between merging companies are not new. In 2018, defence contractor SAIC told staff not to contact workers at Engility, which it was acquiring, without clearance from its integration team. DoorDash has simply taken the idea to LinkedIn.The stakes explain the care. DoorDash is paying $65 a share, a 26% premium to Instacart's October 22 closing price, and the total is more than the $13.7 billion in revenue it reported last year. Card data from Consumer Edge puts DoorDash at 59% of US delivery app spending, while Instacart's share has slipped from 26% to 18% in five years. The deal still needs Instacart shareholder approval and antitrust clearance in the US, Canada and Israel. Regulators have stepped in on grocery before: a federal judge blocked Kroger's $24.6 billion bid for Albertsons in 2024.Until those approvals arrive, a DoorDash employee's reply to an Instacart colleague stays limited to one line of congratulations.
Article Summary: DoorDash has told its employees not to add Instacart staff on LinkedIn while its $17 billion acquisition of the grocery delivery company waits for approval. Antitrust lawyers call it gun-jumping when merging companies behave as if a deal has already closed. DoorDash is paying $65 a share, a 26% premium toinstacart's October 22 closing price.

Article Title: Tech billionaire Kenneth Hao and wife Kathy Chiao commit $175 million to transform healthcare with advanced technology
Article Text:
Breaking down the $175 million commitment

UC San Francisco

($100 million)

UC Davis

($75 million)

Why tech billionaires are pouring into hospital infrastructure

Private equity titan Kenneth Hao and his wife, Kathy Chiao, have pledged at least $175 million to the University of California system to modernise medical infrastructure through cutting-edge technology. The nine-figure philanthropic effort, which was finalised across the first half of the year, targets the integration of next-generation tech, artificial intelligence (AI) and expanded clinical capacity across both human healthcare and veterinary medicine.Hao, who serves as chairman and managing partner of the global technology investment giant Silver Lake, has quietly supported the UC network alongside Chiao for more than a decade. Silver Lake is known for backing major semiconductor players such as Broadcom and Altera. Their latest commitments place them among an expanding group of low-profile tech billionaires directing massive personal fortunes into health-focused capital projects, as per Inside Philanthropy website.The couple’s funding is divided between two flagship Northern California institutions.UCSF is the only campus within the University of California system dedicated exclusively to medical and life sciences research. However, its century-old facilities were never engineered to support the sophisticated machinery, computing power and technological shifts defining modern medicine. Notably, the $100 million gift is structured to address infrastructure hurdles. These include:$50 million for physical modernisation across UCSF’s aging health campus, including the construction of a new hospital building as part of ongoing upgrades at UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland; $40 million to build out advanced technological systems, digital tools and research programs; and $10 million for the Weill Cancer Hub West for the joint cancer research initiative operated in collaboration with Stanford University.The remaining $75 million was directed to UC Davis, home to the UC system’s premier veterinary school. The funding is designated to expand the university's veterinary care facilities by 50%, finance veterinary student scholarships, fund translational medicine research and support community assistance programs for pet owners unable to afford specialised veterinary treatments.For Hao and Chiao, the decision to fund physical facilities alongside digital research stems from a simple reality: breakthrough science cannot function inside obsolete buildings.“There’s an extraordinary revolution in technology, in AI, of course, but also life sciences. With these things happening at the same time, there’s a huge need for modernisation in hospitals. There are never enough advanced hospital beds, and there’s never enough capacity for advanced vet care,” Hao explained.Hao noted that while bricks and mortar may appear secondary to laboratory discoveries, state-of-the-art physical facilities are essential to housing the complex hardware needed to crack difficult medical problems.The couple’s private foundation, The Hao Family Foundation, saw its asset base grow to approximately $304 million by 2024, with the majority of its charitable distributions directed through donor-advised vehicles.
Article Summary: Kenneth Hao and his wife, Kathy Chiao, have pledged at least $175 million to the University of California system to modernise medical infrastructure. The nine- figure philanthropic effort targets the integration of next-generation tech, artificial intelligence (AI) and expanded clinical capacity. The couple’s funding is divided between two flagship Northern California institutions.

Article Title: Microsoft says 'big No' to UK's most-valuable startup Nscale; as Texas datacentre troubles haunt
Article Text:
Microsoft says 'big No' to UK's most-valuable startup Nscale; as Texas datacentre troubles haunt

Why Microsoft rejected Nscale’s Texas data centre deal

Nscale faces growing challenges ahead of IPO

Microsoft has rejected an option to expand its existing deal with Nscale for computing power at a Texas data centre. The update comes as a fresh setback to the UK’s most valuable AI start-up as it prepares for a potential $35 billion stock market listing. The US software giant has decided not to take up an option to lease additional computing capacity worth tens of billions of dollars, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times (FT). As per the report, the decision could force Nscale to find new customers for the site or risk losing billions of dollars in potential future revenue.Nscale had secured a deal with Microsoft in October 2025 to lease around 240MW of computing capacity at a data centre site in Ward County, Texas. The agreement also included an option for Microsoft to lease additional capacity. Nscale later clarified to the FT that the option was closer to 500MW and related to additional capacity at its own site. Microsoft has now decided against taking up that option, according to people familiar with the matter.The development is significant for Nscale, which has the right of first refusal to find customers for an adjacent data centre site being developed by crypto miner Ionic Digital.However, the company has not yet secured power for the remaining capacity at that site. Ionic Digital has reserved the right to offer the expanded energy capacity to other AI, enterprise and cloud infrastructure companies, or use it for its own operations.The setback comes as Nscale, backed by Nvidia and led by former Australian cryptocurrency miner Josh Payne, prepares for a potential IPO this year. The company has also faced challenges at other projects. Earlier this year, Microsoft withdrew from a $3 billion deal to lease computing capacity at Nscale’s data centre in Essex, UK.Its flagship data centre project in West Virginia, which is central to its $45 billion computing deal with Anthropic, has also faced construction delays and opposition from local residents.Nscale is also developing data centre sites in Portugal and Norway to expand its AI infrastructure business.
Article Summary: Nscale had secured a deal with Microsoft in October 2025 to lease around 240MW of computing capacity at a data centre site in Ward County, Texas. The agreement also included an option for Microsoft to lease additional capacity. Nscale later clarified to the FT that the option was closer to 500MW and related to additional capacity at its own site.

Article Title: Qualcomm is selling fewer phone chips, earning less on each and charging more for them
Article Text:
Qualcomm’s phone chip sales drop 26%

Qualcomm’s chip margins are shrinking despite the price hikes

Qualcomm’s biggest Android customers are shipping fewer phones

Qualcomm's smartphone chip business shrank by about a quarter in the September quarter, according to the company's latest earnings report. Handset chip revenue fell 26% to $5.14 billion from $6.96 billion a year ago, wiping out roughly $1.8 billion in sales and missing the StreetAccount estimate of $5.21 billion. Adjusted earnings per share dropped 28% to $2.17, adjusted pre-tax profit fell 30%, and total adjusted revenue slipped 7% to $10.44 billion.Its chips are about to get more expensive too. The Snapdragon maker is raising prices across its products, citing rising costs in wafer fabrication, chip packaging, memory and other materials. It already raised prices in September, and phone chip sales fell anyway. The stock slid as much as 7% in after-hours trading on Wednesday after the company’s forecast for the current quarter came in below expectations. Before the results, it was up just 1.3% for the year.The price increases are not protecting margins yet, and the company says they won’t fully do so until the second half of fiscal 2027, which begins in April. Revenue at its chip division fell 8% to $9.02 billion, and its pre-tax margin dropped to 24% from 29% a year ago. For this quarter, Qualcomm has guided for 20% to 22%. It puts three points of that fall down to folding its data centre unit, which is spending heavily ahead of its revenue ramp, into the chip segment.The full year was no better. Handset chip revenue fell 13% to $24.07 billion in fiscal 2026, about $3.7 billion less than the year before. Adjusted earnings per share dropped 12% to $10.54, and adjusted pre-tax profit fell 16%. The company still spent $7.8 billion buying back its own shares over the year.Licensing, the business that collects royalties from phone makers using the company’s patents, slipped as well. Its revenue fell 7% to $1.3 billion in the quarter, and its profit dropped 10%, even after it renewed licensing deals with Apple, Huawei and Transsion.The forecast offers little comfort. Qualcomm expects adjusted earnings of $2.15 to $2.35 a share this quarter, a midpoint below the $2.27 analysts had pencilled in. It also expects the smartphone market, which still drives most of its chip sales, to stay flat through 2027.The slide in handset revenue mirrors the trouble at the phone makers Qualcomm sells to. Rising memory prices have forced brands to raise prices and cut production. Global smartphone shipments fell 20% year-on-year in the July to September quarter, according to Counterpoint Research. OPPO and Vivo, two of the chipmaker’s major Android customers, each shipped more than 20% fewer phones than a year ago.Xiaomi, another key customer, also cut shipments. It is now using its own XRING O3 chipset to set its premium phones apart, the same segment where Qualcomm sells its most expensive chips.The data centre business Qualcomm wants investors to focus on is being held back as well. CEO Cristiano Amon said the unit is limited by supply. “If I had more supply, I would probably be doing better,” he said.Qualcomm is now asking phone makers to pay more for its chips at a time when they are already struggling to sell phones. By the company’s own timeline, the higher prices won’t fully show up in its margins until April at the earliest.
Article Summary: Handset chip revenue fell 26% to $5.14 billion from $6.96 billion a year ago. Qualcomm is raising prices across its products, citing rising costs in wafer fabrication, chip packaging, memory and other materials. It already raised prices in September, and phone chip sales fell anyway.

Article Text:
From MacKenzie Scott’s surprise donation to long-term strategy

The 10-year plan

Building on 25 years of housing investment

A year after Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gave $30 million to a Silicon Valley-based nonprofit community loan fund Housing Trust Silicon Valley has unveiled a 10-year strategy aimed at turning the one-time gift into lasting housing solutions across the Bay Area. The organisation says the funding will help expand affordable housing initiatives, support first-time homebuyers, strengthen policy advocacy efforts and back innovative housing projects over the next decade. a San Jose-based community loan fund, announced on September 30, 2025, a 10-year plan for turning the unrestricted gift from Scott’s Yield Giving fund into long-term housing solutions across the Bay Area.Housing Trust announced the donation on October 2, 2024. CEO Noni Ramos called it “the largest from an individual in our history” and said it came as a surprise. The gift was unrestricted, which means the nonprofit can decide how to use it, and it was meant to help the organisation expand its work across the 14-county greater Bay Area. At the time, early ideas for the money included seeding a new capital raise for its loan fund, expanding existing programmes and launching new initiatives to deepen partnerships and increase equity and affordability in housing.The release highlighted two recent projects as examples of its work. At Meridian Apartments in Sunnyvale, Housing Trust provided a $2 million predevelopment loan, in partnership with Related California, to help create 90 affordable homes for families. In San Rafael, it supported Eden Housing with a $4 million loan for Vivalon, a 66-unit development for older adults that pairs affordable homes with supportive services.The plan, developed with input from staff, the board and community stakeholders, has five major initiatives:* Lending capital and new products: Expanding the core revolving loan fund and piloting new tools to meet developers’ changing needs. More details were due at the organisation’s Investor Briefing on October 15.* Homeownership expansion: Beginning in 2026, extending first-time homebuyer programmes to reach more households across a wider area.* Policy and partnerships: Hiring new staff to strengthen advocacy and collaboration across sectors that could unlock more resources and affordable housing.* Impact measurement and management: Launching a framework in early 2026 to better track, evaluate and communicate results.* Innovation investments: Supporting mission-driven housing innovations that can reduce costs, shorten development timelines and increase affordability.Noni Ramos CEO of Housing Trust said the gift allows the organisation to take bold steps and carries both the responsibility and the freedom to scale what works, take calculated risks on new ideas and widen its reach. Board Chair Lisa Gutierrez, a senior vice president at U.S. Bank, said the plan is not about one-time dollars but about building momentum that compounds. By putting the funds to work strategically, she said, Housing Trust can attract new partners, expand homeownership and make loans to create and preserve rental housing in ways it could not before, while also strengthening the organisation itself.The announcement comes as Housing Trust Silicon Valley marks its 25th anniversary. Since its founding in 2000, the community development financial institution says it has invested more than $690 million, helped create over 28,700 affordable housing opportunities and supported more than 53,800 residents in finding homes they can afford. The organisation says its work has also leveraged nearly $9 billion in additional public and private capital.Board Chair Lisa Gutierrez said the goal is to use the donation strategically to attract new partners, expand homeownership opportunities and support loans for creating and preserving affordable rental housing, while strengthening the organisation's long-term capacity.The nonprofit said the decade-long strategy is designed to ensure that MacKenzie Scott's donation continues generating impact long after the original gift was received, helping create more affordable and stable housing opportunities across the Bay Area.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gave $30 million to a Silicon Valley-based nonprofit community loan fund Housing Trust Silicon Valley. Article Title: After losing nearly $1 trillion following earnings reports, tech companies gain over $750 billion and the reason is …
Article Text:
Tech companies gain over $750 billion

US midterm results: Big Tech bounces back

Why the midterm sweep sparked Tech stocks’ rally

Data center stocks plunge

Tech giants, including Google-parent Alphabet, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft and others, bounced back, putting five of the world’s largest companies on track to add more than $750 billion in combined market value. The trigger behind the turnaround is the sweeping Democratic victory in the US midterm elections that is said to slow down the pace of artificial intelligence (AI) data-center construction. The rally comes on the heels of a crushing tech sell-off that shaved nearly $1 trillion off the tech-heavy Nasdaq in a single week, and essentially, erasing roughly $2 trillion over the past month.Investors had aggressively dumped Big Tech shares after recent quarterly earnings reports revealed that the fierce race to build AI infrastructure was turning once cash-rich, debt-light powerhouses into heavy spenders increasingly reliant on borrowing. However, as the picture around the US midterm results became clearer, shares across the technology sector surged as trading opened on November 4, according to a report by news agency Reuters.Amazon jumped 7.4% to hit a three-month high, recovering from summer profit misses and spending disclosures that previously dragged the stock down 1.8%.Apple gained nearly 7% to reach an all-time record high. While Apple has largely sidestepped the massive capital expenditure race of its peers, it had recently felt the squeeze of AI-driven memory chip price hikes.Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft – all three advanced between 2% and 6.3%. Microsoft stood out during earnings season with $18.6 billion in cash flow, while Alphabet had previously suffered its worst single-day drop on record, plunging over 12% and shedding $500 billion after burning massive amounts of cash on AI.The rebound was fueled by landslide Democratic wins across the country, particularly in Texas, where resistance to data-center expansion has rapidly gained momentum. Local opposition to the massive, power-hungry, water-intensive and noisy facilities that underpin the AI boom has reached a boiling point. With Democrats taking key seats, investors anticipate that regulatory roadblocks and community pushback will force companies to decelerate their infrastructure rollout.Data center developers and specialised infrastructure providers suffered heavy losses. Shares of smaller operators, including Applied Digital and Iren, plunged between 6% and 13%. Smaller competitors like CoreWeave and Nebius, which have spent multiples of their total revenue to satisfy surging order backlogs, face heightened risks if debt-financed construction projects run into legislative or permitting gridlock, the report noted.
Article Summary: Tech giants, including Google-parent Alphabet, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft and others, bounced back, putting five of the world’s largest companies on track to add more than $750 billion in combined market value. The trigger behind the turnaround is the sweeping Democratic victory in the US midterm elections. The rally comes on the heels of a crushing tech sell-off that shaved nearly $1 trillion off the tech-heavy Nasdaq in a single week, erasing roughly $2 trillion over the past month.

Article Title: Meta has ‘extraordinary’ targets for CEO Mark Zuckerberg: Stock has to double, then double again; And each time, shareholders get…
Article Text:
Zuckerberg’s tax problem, Meta’s share fix

California’s billionaire tax pushed Meta to rework its shares

Meta needs non-voting shares to fund its AI spending

Meta has set a bar for Mark Zuckerberg that the company itself calls “extraordinary.” Each time Meta’s stock doubles, and compounds at least 10% a year along the way, every shareholder gets one free Class C share for each share they own. The condition is written into a Founder Alignment Agreement between Meta and its CEO, which also sets terms for how he sells his new shares and his service at the company. Meta’s stock has already risen more than 1,700% since its IPO, against about 495% for the S&P 500, and the board wants that kind of run to continue.The yardstick is $580.60, Meta’s share price on September 10. In pre-split terms, the first payout kicks in once the stock’s 30-day average price crosses just over $1,161, which would put Meta’s market value close to $3 trillion. The next comes at around $2,322, and the pattern repeats with every doubling after that. This sits on top of the one-for-one Class C dividend Meta has already declared. That takes effect on January 19, 2027, and works much like a two-for-one stock split.The new Class C shares carry no voting rights, and that is by design. Zuckerberg controls about 61% of Meta’s votes through super-voting stock. The new class lets him sell without loosening that grip.He can sell up to 20% of the Class C shares he receives right away, about 10% of his overall economic stake. He also gets the same dividends, on the same terms, as every other shareholder.The rejig traces back to Proposition 40, a California ballot measure proposing a one-time 5% tax on residents worth more than $1 billion. Zuckerberg, the world’s fifth-richest person at roughly $247 billion, had considered leaving the state over it. According to the filing, Meta worried that steps like listing his home for sale could prompt employees to question the company’s leadership.A special committee of the board then negotiated with him, in talks the filing calls “protracted and, at several points, contentious.” Zuckerberg first pitched a 20-for-1 dividend, which the committee rejected as excessive. The final deal ties him to California for eight years while he leads Meta, barring material unforeseen circumstances, and gives him enough sellable stock to cover the tax.Californians voted on Prop 40 on November 3. Counting is still underway and early returns show the measure trailing. The eight-year commitment stands either way.The tax is only part of the story. Meta’s internal forecasts show it will need to raise “hundreds of billions of dollars” over several years for its AI push. Class C shares let it do that without diluting Zuckerberg’s control. The company expects to spend $135 billion to $145 billion on capital expenditure in 2026. It spent $34.91 billion in the third quarter alone and posted negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, its first quarter of cash burn in at least a decade.The core business is still growing fast. Third-quarter revenue rose 26% year on year to $64.6 billion. Its Muse AI assistant has also spent most of its time since September at the top of US app store charts.Investors weren’t thrilled, though. Meta’s shares fell 6% the morning after the announcement. The plan could also face legal pushback: Cloudflare shareholders have sued in Delaware to block a similar non-voting share class. Meta itself dropped a comparable proposal in 2017, days before Zuckerberg was due to testify in a shareholder trial.Meta’s stock has already climbed more than sevenfold from its November 2022 low, to a market value of nearly $1.8 trillion. The doubling clause bets it can pull off a run like that again, this time while spending more on AI than ever.
Article Summary: California's billionaire tax pushed Meta to rework its shares. Each time Meta’s stock doubles, and compounds at least 10% a year along the way, every shareholder gets one free Class C share. The condition is written into a Founder Alignment Agreement between Meta and its CEO.

“I want to grant myself permission to speak fearlessly.”

What GM’s battery bet means for competition with China

“We’re developing this here.”

GM engineers are encouraged to challenge their bosses

“And if there isn’t, then to me that means that they didn’t stretch far enough. So I want to see red.”

Saying no is part of setting priorities

“If you don’t have a list of things you’re not going to do this quarter, then I assume you have too many people,”

General Motors is challenging China’s dominance in EV batteries. Alongside developing a different battery chemistry for electric trucks and large SUVs, the automaker is encouraging engineers to question senior leaders, acknowledge uncertainty and turn down work that distracts from their priorities. According to a Fortune report, that cultural shift helped GM move forward with a battery technology it had spent more than a decade researching.GM has encouraged employees to use this phrase when opening a disagreement with their seniors, Kurt Kelty, its vice president of battery and sustainability, told Fortune. Battery engineer Andy Oury said the approach helped open up the debate over lithium manganese-rich batteries, or LMR, which GM plans to produce commercially with LG Energy Solution in 2028.Much of the world’s inexpensive EV battery supply uses lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, a chemistry dominated by China. GM’s LMR cells replace much of the nickel and cobalt with cheaper, more plentiful manganese and additional lithium.GM says the technology can deliver roughly a third more energy density than leading LFP cells at comparable cost. Higher energy density means batteries can store more energy for their size or weight.Kelty told Fortune.The company’s $900 million investment in battery development facilities in Warren, Michigan, is intended to help engineers develop cells and work out how to manufacture them. Previously, GM relied on partners to turn its cell designs into physical batteries.The commercial outcome remains uncertain. Kelty said GM had enough supporting data to get about 60% to 70% of the way to its LMR decision, with further development needed to close the gap.Kelty described an engineer challenging him during a call with a senior vice president listening.Kelty welcomed the intervention, telling Fortune:The same logic applies to quarterly performance reviews. Kelty, who joined GM in February 2024, implemented measurable goals tracked with red, yellow, and green indicators. He wants some red results because it means employees were aiming for difficult goals.he said.Kelty also asked his direct reports to identify their annual priorities and two things they would not do. Oury said this challenged GM's established instinct to accept every assignment.Kelty said.He said the team took about a year to embrace the change. One example helped: an employee whose review contained numerous red results still received his highest performance ranking.

Article Title: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s tax proposal that will come for houses of Jeff Bezos, Michael Dell and other millionaires clears legal hurdle; what the court says
Article Text:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s tax proposal that will come for houses of Jeff Bezos, Michael Dell and other millionaires clears legal hurdle

New York City administration sent initial notice in July

Zohran Mamdani reacts

New York City Mayor Zohran Mandani scored a legal victory after a state appeals court reversed a lower court ruling that had previously ordered his administration to redo the rollout of a tax on high-end second homes. Called the “pied-à-terre tax”, it would apply to homes worth over $5 million that are not the owner’s main residence. The ruling reverses a previous ruling by Staten Island judge dated September 29 that the city had mishandled the rollout and ordered officials to restart the process. According to a Fox News report, the four judge panel unanimously dismissed the homeowners' lawsuit stating that the plaintiffs lacked legal standing. Under the new ruling, Mamdani’s administration gets a go ahead to continue implementing the surcharge on the ultra-rich.Announced earlier this year, the tax could impact billionaires including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Dell CEO Michael Dell.In a post on X earlier this year in July, Mamdani said owners of second homes in New York City worth more than $5 million should "check your mailbox" because the city has started sending notification letters about its upcoming pied-à-terre tax."If you have a second home in New York City worth more than $5M, check your mailbox when you're back in the five boroughs — because you've got mail," Mamdani wrote in the post dated July 24."Today, we sent notification letters to property owners, letting them know that our new pied-à-terre tax is coming soon."Reacting to the latest ruling, Zohran Mamdani said: “From day one, those with the most have attempted to use every legal avenue available to shield their wealth and avoid contributing more to our city”.Randy Mastro, an attorney representing the homeowners, criticized the court for dismissing the lawsuit without addressing the merits of their challenge. "It’s a shame that, after the City admittedly botched the rollout of this surcharge, the court today took the procedural offramp of standing to avoid addressing the merits of this case," Mastro said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital."What the City has done here is unconscionable — trying to ensnare thousands of people who don’t owe this surcharge into having to prove they live in their own homes or else have to pay it. But now, this lawless and chaotic data collection scheme will go unremedied."
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani scored a legal victory after a state appeals court reversed a lower court ruling that had previously ordered his administration to redo the rollout of a tax on high-end second homes. The ruling reverses a previous ruling by Staten Island judge dated September 29 that the city had mishandled the rollout and ordered officials to restart the process.

Article Title: Uber riders in India may pay more as rising fuel costs hit driver supply
Article Text:
Fuel costs hit drivers in Brazil and India

Uber shifts incentives from riders to drivers

Algorithms decide where the money goes

Strong revenue growth, earnings miss estimates

Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi has warned that riders in markets such as India and Brazil could face higher prices as the ongoing conflict in Iran drives up global fuel costs and puts pressure on driver supply, according to comments made during the company's third-quarter 2026 earnings call. As reported by Benzinga, the ride-hailing giant said rising fuel prices linked to escalating tensions in the Middle East are having a noticeable impact on emerging markets, where both drivers and consumers tend to be more sensitive to price changes. Uber executives indicated that the company is adjusting incentives to maintain driver availability, a move that could result in higher fares for customers.Asked about supply constraints in emerging markets, Chief Financial Officer Balaji Krishnamurthy said the escalation of the Middle East war had pushed up fuel costs worldwide. The effect is felt “materially” in emerging markets, he said, because consumers and drivers there are both sensitive to price. Krishnamurthy singled out Brazil and India, where he said higher fuel prices have meaningfully affected the supply of drivers.Commenting on the situation, Dara Khosrowshahi said Uber operates a flexible incentive system that allows it to balance support between riders and drivers depending on market conditions.According to the CEO, Uber previously directed a larger share of incentives toward riders to reduce prices and encourage demand. This year, however, the company is reducing some rider incentives and redirecting those funds toward driver incentives to help offset the impact of rising fuel costs and maintain marketplace balance.The shift could lead to higher ride prices for customers as Uber attempts to ensure sufficient driver availability while protecting profitability. "We will do trade-offs against profitability, but that is something that we handle," Khosrowshahi said, explaining that the company constantly adjusts incentives based on supply and demand conditions.Khosrowshahi further emphasised that the data science and algorithms play a major role in the decision-making process at Uber. He added that the system at Uber analyse billions of trips to decide where the incentives should go, enabling the company to optimise the spending between the riders and drivers more effectively. As per Khosrowshahi, these algorithms also help the company in responding quickly to the changing dynamics of market, including fuel-price and driver shortages.Uber reported third-quarter revenue of $14.77 billion, up 10% year-over-year and above Wall Street expectations of $14.70 billion. However, adjusted earnings per share came in at 88 cents, missing analysts' consensus estimate of 91 cents. The company also repurchased $750 million worth of shares during the quarter, while gross bookings increased 20% year-over-year to $59.8 billion, reflecting continued growth across its ride-hailing and delivery businesses.
Article Summary: Ride-hailing giant said rising fuel prices linked to escalating tensions in the Middle East are having a noticeable impact on emerging markets. Uber executives indicated that the company is adjusting incentives to maintain driver availability. The shift could lead to higher ride prices for customers as Uber attempts to ensure sufficient driver availability while protecting profitability.

Article Title: CERT-In issues critical alert on AI-powered cyberattacks targeting banks, fintech firms
Article Text:
Who is being targeted

Repeat attacks

AI tools behind the attacks

How the attacks work

What firms are told to do

India’s cyber agency CERT-In has issued a critical-severity advisory on a growing campaign of AI-assisted attacks on banks, lenders and payment firms. It warns that the threat is active and still escalating. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0058, was issued on November 4. It updates an October 9 advisory (CIAD-2026-0046) on attackers exploiting payment and disbursement APIs to make unauthorised fund transfers. CERT-In said continued analysis of reported incidents showed a significant escalation since then.The affected entities include non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech firms, payment aggregators and payment service providers. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers are also on the list.CERT-In’s financial-sector response team, CSIRT-Fin, has named the attacker “CRAFTY FALCON.” It describes the actor as AI-assisted, one that surveys targets with machine intelligence, works at machine speed and strikes by calling the victim’s own payment and disbursement APIs.CSIRT-Fin continues to receive reports of successful attacks.These include entities that had received earlier restricted advisories and had already carried out remediation. Some firms were deliberately attacked again after incomplete clean-ups, and attacks were timed for holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection.CERT-In said the attackers are using several publicly available AI offensive-security tools, including the ARTEX family of LLM-based tools, the PentAGI autonomous multi-agent penetration testing system, the Cairn attack search engine and the CyberStrikeAI framework. The agency said these tools run complete attack chains on their own, generate and refine large numbers of tailored scripts in quick succession, and adapt payloads based on how the target responds. The attackers’ infrastructure changes IP addresses within hours or days.The advisory lists these patterns:* Cloud abuse: Attackers misuse cloud management and serverless services, such as AWS Systems Manager and Lambda, to run commands and deploy malicious files, blending in with legitimate activity.* Weak entry points: Internet-exposed test and staging environments are used as a way in, then attackers move to production using shared credentials, tokens or network paths.* Tampered apps: Attackers reverse-engineer application code and send unauthorised API calls using modified app packages, defeating controls that assume only the genuine app will call the APIs.* Allow-list bypass: Traffic is routed through shared third-party fetcher services, such as content-acceleration and app-store review fetchers, to get around IP allow-lists.* Test transactions: Attackers send micro-value payments, such as Rs 1, to check that unauthorised fund flows work before moving large sums.* Settlement APIs: Merchant settlement APIs at payment aggregators are abused to move money.* Fast exploitation of new flaws: Newly published vulnerabilities, including file-upload and deserialisation flaws, are exploited as soon as they become public, leading to web shells in PHP and Node.js applications.* Crypto theft: Wallet keys are stolen from crypto exchanges and funds siphoned out.* AI-generated scripts: Large numbers of near-identical custom scripts appear in quick succession, a pattern CERT-In says is consistent with AI-generated code.CERT-In asked financial entities to treat the campaign as an immediate and continuing threat. Its recommendations include:* 24x7 monitoring with extra staffing and lower alert thresholds on holidays and weekends.* Assuming attackers persist after any incident, with full forensic clean-up and regular threat hunting.* Strict separation of test and staging environments from production.* Server-side validation of every transaction, API request signing and app attestation, rather than trusting client apps.* Replacing IP allow-listing of shared fetcher pools with identity-based controls such as mutual TLS or signed requests.* Flagging micro-value test payments to new beneficiaries followed by large transfers, and holding or reviewing those flows.* Maker-checker approval and reconciliation for merchant settlement instructions.* Hardware security modules or cold storage and multi-signature approvals for crypto wallet keys.* Banning unauthorised AI offensive tools on corporate systems and watching for LLM API traffic from servers.* Rapid patching of internet-facing applications, honeypots and canary credentials as early-warning measures, and zero-trust architecture.
Article Summary: India’s cyber agency CERT-In has issued a critical-severity advisory on a growing campaign of AI-assisted attacks on banks, lenders and payment firms. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0058, was issued on November 4. It updates an October 9 advisory on attackers exploiting payment and disbursement APIs to make unauthorised fund transfers.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos gave Eva Longoria and Bill McRaven $100 million, but she challenges the belief that giving back requires wealth, saying ‘impact doesn’t come from how much money you have’
Article Text:
How Jeff Bezos brought Eva Longoria and Bill McRaven together

Why Eva Longoria believes giving back is about more than money

What Longoria has done with her philanthropic award

What Bill McRaven plans to do with his $50 million

Growing debate over billionaire philanthropy and public responsibility

Philanthropy is often associated with people who have fortunes large enough to fund schools, charities and ambitious social programmes. Yet the ability to support others does not necessarily depend on the size of a bank account. As reported by Fortune, actress Eva Longoria has been making that distinction after receiving a $50 million philanthropic award from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos, alongside retired US Navy admiral Bill McRaven. Two years after the recognition, Longoria says the experience has changed how she approaches charitable work, but she also wants to challenge the idea that meaningful contributions are reserved for wealthy individuals.In 2024, Eva Longoria and retired admiral Bill McRaven were selected as recipients of the Bezos Courage and Civility Award, an initiative established by Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos to recognise people working to improve society.“The Courage and Civility Award makes it possible for us at the Eva Longoria Foundation to create long-term impact with transformative giving.”Each recipient received $50 million, bringing the combined philanthropic commitment to $100 million.The funding was intended to support causes that reflected their respective areas of work.For Longoria, the award offered an opportunity to expand programmes focused on education, economic opportunities and support for Latino communities in the United States. McRaven, meanwhile, had plans to direct his share towards education and support services for military personnel and their families.McRaven is widely recognised for overseeing the 2011 US military operation that resulted in the death of al Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden.Longoria's experience with the award has given her a larger platform to discuss charitable giving, but her message is not centred on financial donations. In an interview with Fortune, she said, “This award has allowed me to continue investing those resources into the communities and causes I care deeply about—supporting Latina entrepreneurs, expanding access to education, and backing organizations that are driving real change on the ground. ”Her understanding of giving back includes mentoring, sharing professional knowledge and helping small businesses find opportunities they might otherwise struggle to access.Longoria's involvement in charitable work began well before she received recognition from Bezos. In 2012, she established the Eva Longoria Foundation, which focuses on improving educational and entrepreneurial opportunities for Latinas in the United States. Its work includes helping women access resources that can support their education and participation in business. She also founded Eva's Heroes, an organisation that supports young adults with intellectual special needs.The $50 million award has provided additional resources for these efforts. Longoria has described the funding as an opportunity to plan longer-term programmes and direct investment towards communities and organisations working on the ground.Her charitable activities also sit alongside a varied business career. The former Desperate Housewives actress has developed interests in entertainment, entrepreneurship and sports, including her luxury tequila brand Casa Del Sol, production company Hyphenate Media Group and investment in women's football club Angel City FC.She has also been associated with an early investment in the John Wick film franchise. These business activities have helped establish her as more than an actor, while her foundation work has remained a separate part of her public life. Longoria has said,“Receiving that support was incredibly meaningful, not just because of the scale of the gift, but because it represented trust and responsibility.”The other half of the $100 million commitment went to Bill McRaven, whose philanthropic priorities reflect his military background. McRaven has said he intends to support educational programmes for future military leaders and children of deceased veterans. Mental health assistance for serving military personnel is another area included in his plans.A former four-star admiral, McRaven held senior leadership positions in the US military and later served as chancellor of the University of Texas System. His work has included military education, leadership development and public service.The Bezos Courage and Civility Award has previously recognised other prominent figures involved in humanitarian and social initiatives. Among its recipients are civil rights advocate Van Jones, chef and humanitarian José Andrés, and singer Dolly Parton.Large charitable donations attract attention because they can finance projects that would be difficult for smaller organisations to undertake. But the concentration of philanthropic resources among a relatively small number of wealthy individuals has also raised questions about how much responsibility should rest with them. The Giving Pledge is one example of an effort to encourage large-scale charitable commitments. Established in 2010 by Bill Gates, Melinda French Gates and Warren Buffett, it invites billionaires to commit at least half of their wealth to charitable causes during their lifetimes or through their wills.More than 250 individuals and families have signed the pledge since its launch. However, making a commitment and distributing the promised wealth are not the same thing. For Liz Baker, chief executive of Greater Good Charities, waiting for wealthy donors to address community problems leaves too much work undone. The organisation she leads has distributed more than $1 billion in support across 121 countries since 2006. Speaking to Fortune, Baker argued that charitable participation should not be limited to people capable of making substantial financial contributions.
Article Summary: Actress Eva Longoria received a $50 million philanthropic award from Jeff Bezos. She was given the award alongside retired US Navy admiral Bill McRaven. Longoria says the experience has changed how she approaches charitable work. She also wants to challenge the idea that meaningful contributions are reserved for wealthy individuals.
